passages.title: A Genealogical Presentation of the Tribes of Israel.
passages.text: The genealogies of chs. 1–9 are intended to show the Chronicler’s generation, now existing as the small province of Yehud (Judah) in the Persian Empire, that they are still God’s people Israel and retain their central place in God’s purposes. They are traced from Adam ( 1:1 ), through the tribes of Israel (chs. 2–8 ), to the community of Judean exiles restored from captivity in Babylon ( 9:2–34 ). The genealogies have been structured to show how the Chronicler conceived of Israel:

passages.title: Adam to Esau.
passages.text: This first genealogy begins with Adam, the first human, then focuses on Isaac’s son Esau and the kings who descended from him.

passages.title: 1 Chron 1:1–4
passages.text: From Genesis 5 . Israel’s direct ancestral link with **Adam** means Israel is the focus of God’s purpose from creation.

passages.title: 1 Chron 1:5–27
passages.text: From Gen. 10:1–29 ; 11:10–32 . Israel is located within the nations, which are also God’s creation and part of his purpose for Israel. The line continues through **Abraham**, who received covenantal promises ( 1 Chron. 16:16 ; 2 Chron. 20:7 ).

passages.title: 1 Chron 1:28–34
passages.text: From Gen. 25:1–4 , 12–16 . The **concubine** ( 1 Chron. 1:32 ) could have the status of a wife.

passages.title: 1 Chron 1:35–54
passages.text: From Gen. 36:10–14 , 20–28 , 31–43 . The descendants of **Esau** and the** sons of Seir** (the Edomites) are grouped together because both inhabited Edom. The latter would often be in conflict with Judah ( 2 Chron. 20:10 ; 21:8 ; 25:5–13 ; 28:17 ).

passages.title: The United Kingdom of David and Solomon.
passages.text: Chron. 10:1–2 Chron. 9:31 The second major section of 1–2 Chronicles concerns the reigns of David and Solomon over Israel. Their rule is presented as a unity; David makes the essential preparations for what Solomon completes.
